decision.explanation: Set f(x)=0: \sqrt[3]{5x+12}=3. Cubing gives 5x+12=27, so 5x=15 and x=3.

after.name: Question 1
after.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
\sqrt[3]{5x+12}-3=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[3]{5x+12}-3 & =0 \\ \sqrt[3]{5x+12} & =3 \\ (\sqrt[3]{5x+12})^{3} & ={3}^{3} \\ 5x+12 & =27 \\ 5x & =15 \\ x & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=3.$

decision.explanation: Setting f(x)=0 gives \sqrt[6]{11-5x}=1. Raising both sides to the sixth power yields 11-5x=1, so x=2. The radicand is then 1, verifying the root.

after.name: Question 2
after.worked_solution:
To find the roots of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
\sqrt[6]{11-5x}-1=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{11-5x}-1 & =0 \\ \sqrt[6]{11-5x} & =1 \\ (\sqrt[6]{11-5x})^{6} & ={1}^{6} \\ 11-5x & =1 \\ -5x & =-10 \\ x & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{11-5\cdot 2}-1 & =0 \\ \sqrt[6]{1}-1 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=2.$

after.name: Question 3
after.worked_solution:
To find the root of $f(x),$  we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
-3\sqrt[6]{2x-5}-3=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-3\sqrt[6]{2x-5}-3 & =0 \\ -3\sqrt[6]{2x-5} & =3 \\ \sqrt[6]{2x-5} & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

This equation does not have any solutions since its left-hand side is always nonnegative, while the right-hand side is negative.

Therefore, $f(x)$ has no root.

decision.explanation: Set f(x)=0 to obtain \sqrt[6]{24x+13}=1. Raising both sides to the sixth power gives 24x+13=1, so x=-12/24=-1/2. Substitution gives a radicand of 1, confirming the root.

after.name: Question 4
after.worked_solution:
To find the roots of $f(x),$ we must solve $f(x)=0:$

$$
\sqrt[6]{24x+13}-1=0
$$

We solve this equation by making $x$ the subject, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{24x+13}-1 & =0 \\ \sqrt[6]{24x+13} & =1 \\ {(\sqrt[6]{24x+13})}^{6} & ={1}^{6} \\ 24x+13 & =1 \\ 24x & =-12 \\ x & =-\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we must check the answer by substituting it back into the initial equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt[6]{24\cdot (-\frac{1}{2})+13}-1 & =0 \\ \sqrt[6]{1}-1 & =0 \\ 0 & =0\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the root of $f(x)$ is $x=-\frac{1}{2}.$
